title: Decide the agent-quality metric spec and build approach
summary: Land a DECISIONS.md entry defining Groundedness/Coherence/Fluency/Relevance (1-5 scale) and task-completion Pass1/Pass5 per current Microsoft Foundry docs and the AgentEval paper, and decide to reimplement as native judge prompts rather than depend on azure-ai-evaluation.
description:
Re-verify live (do not rely on a prior conversation's cached summary) the current Microsoft Foundry built-in-evaluator definitions at learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/concepts/built-in-evaluators: Groundedness, Coherence, Fluency, and Relevance as 1-5 LLM-judged scores, plus the agent-specific Intent Resolution and Task Adherence evaluators. Cross-check against the AutoGen AgentEval paper (Arabzadeh et al., arXiv 2402.09015) for its multi-criteria task-utility framing (accuracy, clarity, efficiency, completeness) and CriticAgent/QuantifierAgent/VerifierAgent methodology, and against Microsoft's STATE-Bench Pass¹/Pass⁵ terminology (opensource.microsoft.com/blog/2026/05/19/introducing-state-bench-a-benchmark-for-ai-agent-memory). Record exact definitions, scales, and verification date in DECISIONS.md — this repo's own EPIC-11 precedent explicitly flags that vendor evaluator sets churn (two Foundry evaluator-set changes already tracked in 2026) and treats unverified specifics as needing re-check before external-facing use; follow the same discipline here.

Decide build approach: implement these as new judge prompts against the existing local-LLM judge pattern (`benchmarks/retrieval_quality/run.py`'s OllamaJudge, proven at BENCH-1/BM-18) rather than adding `azure-ai-evaluation` as a hard dependency. Rationale to record: (1) this SDK's benchmark philosophy per BENCHMARK_STRATEGY.md is to assemble maintained *benchmark infrastructure* (pytest-benchmark, Locust, LongMemEval) but the LLM-judge logic itself has always been hand-rolled (OllamaJudge), so a new judge dimension is additive to an existing pattern, not a new category of dependency; (2) the `agent-framework` optional extra's own pyproject.toml comment records that a Microsoft package was not reliably installable in this environment as recently as 2026-08-02 — treat a second Microsoft SDK dependency as a repeat of that same risk until proven otherwise; (3) `azure-ai-evaluation`'s evaluators assume an Azure-hosted judge model by default, which conflicts with this project's local-Ollama-judge, zero-mandatory-cloud-infra Step 0 philosophy.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- DECISIONS.md entry with verification date, exact metric names/scales, and the explicit build-vs-depend decision with the three rationale points above (or a corrected rationale if live verification changes the picture).
- No code changes in this story.

**Definition of Done:**
- DECISIONS.md entry merged.
- Blocks AGQ-2/AGQ-3/AGQ-4 (they need the metric definitions this story finalizes); does not block UNI-1 (which only needs the *existence* of the gap, not the finalized spec).
